name: Shitala Mata Temple, Butapaldi
significance: A small twelfth-century shrine of the goddess Shitala in the Mehsana district village of Butapaldi, where she is worshipped under the local name Brahmani. It is protected by the state of Gujarat as monument S-GJ-286 and survives as a modest example of Maru-Gurjara temple building in north Gujarat.

name: Ved Mata Gaytri Mandir
significance: A recently built Hindu temple at Kushinagar in eastern Uttar Pradesh dedicated to Gayatri, the goddess who personifies the Vedic Gayatri mantra. It was founded by Rampravesh Kushwaha and opened on 8 December 2013.

name: Alavaimalai Subrayar Murugan Temple
significance: A hill shrine of Murugan on Alavaimalai near Alavaipatti in the Vennandur block of Namakkal district, built in the Dravidian manner and served by a climb to the summit sanctum.

name: Mahakal Temple, Darjeeling
significance: A hilltop shrine of Shiva above Darjeeling, raised in 1782 by Lama Dorjey Rinzing on the site of the Dorje-Ling monastery of 1765 from which the town takes its name. Hindu and Buddhist worship are carried on together at the same site.
story: Three Shiva lingams standing for Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva are said to have manifested themselves on the hill in 1782.

name: Radha Madhab Temple, Bishnupur
significance: A brick ek-ratna temple of Radha and Krishna founded at Bishnupur in 1737 by Churamoni, wife of the Mallabhum ruler Bir Singha Dev. Its terracotta facing carries scenes of the Krishna lila together with Dashavatara panels and floral ornament.

name: Goravanahalli Mahalakshmi Temple
significance: A much-visited shrine of the goddess Mahalakshmi in the Tumkur district village of Goravanahalli in Karnataka. Its worship was sustained through the twentieth century by the devotee Kamalamma, who came to the village in 1925 and settled there in 1952.
story: The goddess is said to have blessed a poor man named Abbayya with wealth, and later to have appeared to Thotadappa in his dreams asking him to raise a shrine for her.

name: Karinjeshwara Temple
place: Karinja, Bantwal taluk, Dakshina Kannada district
significance: A hill temple in Bantwal taluk of Dakshina Kannada, completed in 1200 CE, where Shiva is worshipped at the summit with Parvati and Ganesha in shrines on the slope below. Feeding the resident troop of monkeys is part of the daily ritual.

name: Venugopalaswamy Temple, Karvetinagaram
significance: A Vaishnavite temple at Karvetinagaram in Chittoor district where Krishna is worshipped as Venugopala, the flute player, with Rukmini and Satyabhama beside him. It was built by King Venkataperumal of the Venkataraja line.

name: Ithiyapuram Kaavu
significance: A sacred-grove shrine (kaavu) on the Kanyakumari-Thiruvananthapuram highway about 30 km from Nagercoil, where Vana Sastha and Vana Durga are the chief deities alongside Bala Ganapati, Nagaraja and Krishna. A copper plate said to have been granted by the Travancore ruler Marthanda Varma is kept there.
story: Devotees hold that Vana Durga came here from the deep forest of Pechiparai, followed by troops of serpents, to stand guard over Vana Sastha.

name: Maa Tara Chandi Temple
significance: A cave shrine of the goddess Tara Chandi set in the Kaimur hills at Sasaram in Bihar, counted among the Shakta seats of the region and drawing large crowds at Navratri.
story: The right eye of Sati's corpse is said to have fallen at this spot when Vishnu cut the body apart with his Sudarshana chakra.

name: Gupteshwar Mahadev, Udaipur
significance: A Shiva shrine set inside a cave near the top of a hill at Titardi village on the outskirts of Udaipur. Pilgrims reach it by a climb of roughly 800 metres from the road, and darshan is offered from morning to late afternoon.

name: Old Madiwala Someshwara Temple
significance: One of the oldest surviving temples in Bengaluru, a Shiva shrine of the Chola period at Madiwala whose stone inscriptions name the reigns of Rajendra Chola and of Ballala III. A large, finely proportioned granite Nandi faces the sanctum across a hall of carved pillars.

name: Sree Kattayattu Bhagavathi Kshethram
deity: Devi as Moovanthikkali and Arayil Bhagavathi
significance: A Bhagavathi temple in the village of Peruvayal near Kozhikode, where the goddess is worshipped in two forms, Moovanthikkali and Arayil Bhagavathi, with Ganapathi and Ayyappa as attendant deities. Its ritual year turns on the Paattulsavam and the Thottam performances.

name: Sathya Vageeswarar Temple, Kalakkad
significance: A Shaivite temple of three precincts at the centre of Kalakkad town in Tirunelveli district, first raised by the Pandyas in the 13th century. Nayak rulers added its pillared halls and principal shrines in the 15th and 16th centuries, and Boothala Veera Udaya Marthanda Varman gave the musical pillared halls at the front.

name: Vedarajan Temple, Thirunagari
significance: A Vishnu temple at Thirunagari in Mayiladuthurai district where the deity is worshipped as Vedarajan and Lakshmi as Amruthavalli. Held to have been begun by the Cholas, it received its pillared halls and larger shrines from Vijayanagara and Thanjavur Nayak patrons in the 16th century.
story: Karthama Prajapathi is said to have done penance here for Lakshmi, who hid in the temple tank among the lotuses; he was born again as prince Sangabalan and became the poet-saint Thirumangai Alvar after being given the sacred mantra.

name: Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, Penna Ahobilam
place: Penna Ahobilam, Uravakonda mandal, Anantapur district
significance: A hill temple of Lakshmi Narasimha at Penna Ahobilam in Anantapur district, built up under Vijayanagara patronage with gopurams, mandapas and subsidiary shrines around the main sanctum. The Vijayanagara king Sadashivaraya is credited with installing the large image and enlarging the complex.
story: A cow is said to have emptied her milk each day into a well on the hill, and when Narasimha appeared and claimed her the cry of wonder, Aho Balam - what power! - gave the place its name.

name: Navapashanam Temple
significance: A shore shrine at Devipattinam on the Ramanathapuram coast where nine stones set in the shallow sea are worshipped as the Navagrahas, the nine planetary deities. Worshippers reach them from the beach when the tide is low.
story: Rama is said to have installed the nine planets here with his own hands, shaping them from the clay of the shore, as part of the worship he offered before crossing to Lanka.

name: Kasi Viswanathar Temple, Sivakasi
significance: The temple from which Sivakasi takes its name, a Shiva shrine with a three-tiered gopuram in Virudhunagar district. It is held to have been built by the Pandya ruler Harikesari Parakkirama Pandian in the 16th century and was extended later by the Madurai Nayaks.
story: A Pandya king is said to have carried a lingam home from Kasi, and where the cow bearing it halted and would not move he understood Shiva's wish and set the lingam down.

name: Arulmigu Prasanna Venkatesa Perumal Temple
significance: A Vishnu temple in the village of Thirupparkadal in Ranipet district, where the god is worshipped as Prasanna Venkateshvara. The Vijayanagara emperor Krishnadevaraya is recorded as having renovated it.
story: Vishnu is said to have come to a devotee here in the guise of an old Vaishnava on an Ekadashi day, and to have revealed himself standing upon a Shiva lingam.

name: Walajapet Kasiviswanathar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in the Walajapet neighbourhood of Ranipet in northern Tamil Nadu, built about three hundred years ago, where the god is worshipped as Kasiviswanathar alongside the goddess Kasivisalakshi.

name: Saumyakeshava Temple, Nagamangala
significance: A Hoysala temple of the 12th century in the Mandya district town of Nagamangala, named for its six-foot image of Keshava, a serene form of Vishnu. Laid out on a stellate plan with northern nagara elements, it drew continued patronage from later rulers including the Vijayanagara emperors.

name: Jagannath Govinda Temple, Hojai
significance: A Vaishnava temple at Gauranagar in the Hojai district of central Assam, established in 1928, where Jagannath and Govinda are worshipped together.

name: Mandagapattu Tirumurti Temple
significance: A rock-cut cave shrine at Mandagapattu in Viluppuram district, excavated for Brahma, Shiva and Vishnu and attributed to the Pallava king Mahendravarman I. It is the oldest stone shrine in Tamil Nadu to have been discovered and securely dated.

name: Mangala Devi Temple, Kagpur
significance: A ruined goddess temple in Kagpur village on State Highway 19, some 33 km from Vidisha, raised in the Paramara period between the 10th and 11th centuries. Its flat-roofed mandapa stands on twelve pillars, and the image of Mangala Devi it houses was installed in 1306.

name: Radha Raman Temple, Vrindavan
significance: One of the oldest surviving temples of Vrindavan in Mathura district, established around 1542 by Gopala Bhatta Goswami, where Krishna is worshipped as Radha Ramana. The shrine is built in the Rajasthani manner.
story: The deity is said to have emerged of its own accord from a Damodara shaligrama stone, which took on the three-fold bending form of Krishna.
